target_customer: Small food retailers such as corner markets that host a sandwich kiosk, and walk-up lunch customers
problem: Lunch lines and wrong orders at food counters; the company pitched an automated sandwich maker customers could watch.
business_model: Hardware kiosk placed in retail locations, with per-sandwich sales ($2 peanut butter sandwich in the first deployment)

founders.name: Jay Reppert
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CEO with no biography. Education and prior employers not found.

exit.reason: Not public. YC lists the company as inactive; no post-mortem or press report found.

technical_complexity.rationale: A small team had to build custom robotic hardware that handled bread, spreads and food safety, with a tablet ordering kiosk. A 2016 write-up said the machine needed repeated repairs, which shows how hard reliability was.

defensibility.rationale: No patents or data advantage were found. The value was in a working machine and retail placements, which a funded rival could copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No sources show any incumbent reacting. The company appears to have stalled on its own.

market_need_then: Retail lunch demand and labor cost were the stated pitch (no lines, no wrong orders). The first deployment sold a $2 sandwich at a San Francisco market in November 2015. No data on sales volume was found.

branding.domain_note: Original bistrobot.com domain; by 2026 it redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale page, so the domain is parked and unused.

brand_strength.rationale: Almost no press about the brand itself was found beyond the product coverage. Name says what it is (bistro plus robot) but nothing shows the brand drove attention.

outcome_analysis: The cause of the shutdown is not public. The company raised only about $170K per one database, installed a first sandwich robot in November 2015 and had reliability problems documented in 2016. The facts are consistent with a hardware startup that could not fund or stabilise its product, but no source states a reason, so no failure factor is assigned.
notes: Funding rests on a single database (CB Insights): $170K total over two rounds, Seed II of $0.12M on 2015-08-20 and an earlier July 2014 seed with no amount; CB lists Y Combinator and Carnegie Mellon University as investors without saying which round. The implied earlier amount is about $50K but is not stated. The Bernalwood article names Hamid Sani as CTO but does not call him a co-founder, so he is not listed as a founder. bistrobot.com redirects to a domain-for-sale page, treated as a dead site. Competitor search found no dated rivals near the 2015 batch, so the list is empty. The Hackaday 2016 page was only seen as a search result.
